chapter: Race, critics and the big bands
title: Jay McShann's raggedy band with Bird and patio dances at home
summary: Sam wanted to hear McShann's band with Parker, Ramey and Gus Johnson, and remembers outdoor patio dances.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: He had a good band, you see. But the band that I always wanted to hear and never got a chance to hear them
*Possibly either Warren Evans or Jimmy Lewis; Evans recorded more with Johnson during the early 1940s, with Lewis as a backup.
when they came through there in Kansas City, you know. Hooty and them...
McShann?
Jay McShann went through there with Bird. Bird was in his saxophone section, and Ramey.
Gene Ramey.
Ramey was playing the bass. I think it was Gus Johnson on drums.
I know Gus was in that band at the time with Gene and Bird.
The band was raggedy, homes. All we had to do was have pasteboard stands, you know. I remember just like it was yesterday man.
Uh huh. (laughs)
And they had some - there used to be a style when that sleeves used to be puffed. Do you remember that style?
Yeah.
That was the kind of suits them dudes had. And them dudes had them konks on. The greasy stuff was all on them, on the collars. I remember that man.
They let them hang through that when they lay down.
But boy them dudes played some music that night man. And see down in my home they had patios you know.
Uh huh.
You know dances with no top, patios.
Uh huh.

You know I wonder why—they couldn't have this kind of stuff up here because there would be weather, you know. But all of the bands used to come, you know. And sometimes they would be indoors at a crosstown dancehall but most of the time, especially in the summertime, man, all of the dances would be played out on the patio.
Uh huh.
Yeah, I experienced all that. I saw all that stuff.
